brief.headline: Close the ₹8.48 L price gap and bring in a qualified second source — their finances aren't public so dual-sourcing is essential supply security

priceAsk.summary: Match the best price we already pay for the same items
priceAsk.target: ₹7.62/NOS on the amber 250 mL bottle (currently ₹8.49/NOS) — an 11.5% cut — to close the ₹8.48 L annual gap
priceAsk.basis: We already buy identical rigid plastic packaging from TPAC Packaging India Pvt Ltd. at ₹7.62/NOS and from Suraj Blow Plast PVt. Ltd. at ₹5.24/NOS. PIK Plastics must match these prices — there's no reason to pay more for the same thing.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Hold at 30 Days After Receipt — no change

brief.financialLeverage: PIK Plastics publishes no financial statements, so we cannot see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. That makes them a higher supply risk. Our ₹1.92 Cr spend is meaningful but we have no visibility into whether it's 5% or 50% of their business. Because we can't gauge their stability, we need to line up a robust second source before we push hard on price. The open market shows caps at ₹0.85–0.95/pc (modest room to ₹0.65–0.80 at volume), so there is headroom — but the real lever is that we already pay less elsewhere, and we must insist they meet that.

evidence.point: We overpay PIK Plastics by ₹8.48 L every year versus the best prices we already have
The biggest item — amber 250 mL bottle — costs us ₹8.49/NOS from PIK but only ₹7.62/NOS from TPAC, an 11.5% gap costing ₹7.19 L a year
Another bottle (BRUT 250 mL/28 mm neck) is ₹5.38/NOS from PIK versus ₹5.24/NOS from Suraj Blow Plast — a 2.6% gap costing ₹1.29 L
Market research shows 28 mm PP caps trade at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with modest volume headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc — the verdict is MARKET-FAIR with room to negotiate

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter — makes pharma bottles, caps and preforms; revenue ₹2569.83 Cr, health score B (65/100) — a strong, proven second-source candidate

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-packaging leader (pails, containers, pharma focus); strong and profitable — a robust alternate for bottles and closures

alternates.name: Pearl Polymers Ltd
alternates.why: Listed PET bottle and jar specialist (Pearlpet brand) — a direct fit for our PET bottle needs

risks: PIK Plastics does not publish financials — we have zero visibility into their stability or cash position, so supply continuity is an unknown
Our ₹1.92 Cr spend could be a large share of their business or a small one — we don't know, so gauge their reaction carefully when you push on price
If we squeeze too hard without a qualified backup live, we risk a disruption; bring Manjushree or Mold-Tek to RFQ stage in parallel
We already have better prices from two other suppliers (TPAC and Suraj) — use those as the floor, but make sure PIK knows we will move volume if they don't match
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the relationship, but we're paying ₹8.48 L more each year than we do for identical items from other suppliers — let's talk about closing that gap and getting your pricing in line with TPAC and Suraj.
